\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2008 SCORING GUIDELINES}

\section*{Question 6}

Let \(f\) be the function given by \(f(x)=\frac{\ln x}{x}\) for all \(x>0\). The derivative of \(f\) is given by \(f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1-\ln x}{x^{2}}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=e^{2}\).
\item[(b)] Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the critical point of \(f\). Determine whether this point is a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither for the function \(f\). Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] The graph of the function \(f\) has exactly one point of inflection. Find the \(x\)-coordinate of this point.
\item[(d)] Find \(\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x)\).
\item[(a)] \(f\left(e^{2}\right)=\frac{\ln e^{2}}{e^{2}}=\frac{2}{e^{2}}, f^{\prime}\left(e^{2}\right)=\frac{1-\ln e^{2}}{\left(e^{2}\right)^{2}}=-\frac{1}{e^{4}}\) An equation for the tangent line is \(y=\frac{2}{e^{2}}-\frac{1}{e^{4}}\left(x-e^{2}\right)\).
\item[(b)] \(f^{\prime}(x)=0\) when \(x=e\). The function \(f\) has a relative maximum at \(x=e\) because \(f^{\prime}(x)\) changes from positive to negative at \(x=e\).
\item[(c)] \(f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\frac{-\frac{1}{x} x^{2}-(1-\ln x) 2 x}{x^{4}}=\frac{-3+2 \ln x}{x^{3}}\) for all \(x>0\) \(f^{\prime \prime}(x)=0\) when \(-3+2 \ln x=0\) \(x=e^{3 / 2}\)
The graph of \(f\) has a point of inflection at \(x=e^{3 / 2}\) because \(f^{\prime \prime}(x)\) changes sign at \(x=e^{3 / 2}\).
\item[(d)] \(\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{\ln x}{x}=-\infty\) or Does Not Exist
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: f\left(e^{2}\right) \text { and } f^{\prime}\left(e^{2}\right) \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x=e \\ 1: \text { relative maximum } \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: f^{\prime \prime}(x) \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[1] : answer
\end{itemize}
